review.notes:
Conflicting evidence preserved: the pre-errata cdb text ('Discard 2 cards, then target 1 face-up monster; change that target to face-down in the same position.') matches no lineage version literally - it is a PSCT paraphrase - and the packet's fuzzy matcher pointed it at v2 (ratio 0.7411), which is the wrong version. I assign historical_text_version 1 on behavioural grounds: 'in the same position' is v1's 'do not change its battle position', and the script's POS_FACEDOWN_ATTACK branch can only correspond to v1. Note also that this packet's lineage indices start at 1, with no index 0 present. Dating caveat, stated rather than resolved: v2 is dated only by the 2023-04-20 Spell Ruler (25th Anniversary Edition) reprint, so the recorded date is when the new text became available in print, not necessarily when the ruling changed; it may have moved earlier via the card database. That does not affect either period format - both the 2005 and 2010 snapshots sit well before any plausible date, and the Edison community source independently attests the position-preserving behaviour in 2010. The remaining diff lines (CATEGORY_SET announcement, REASON_COST|REASON_DISCARD vs +, the SetOperationInfo position argument) are announcement/notation only.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Darkness Approaches). The rulings read support d1 at both snapshots (the passages are in the check); nothing contradicts a claimed difference, so kind, summary and coverage are unchanged. Verdicts: [event] d1 supported at Edison, supported at Tengu.

effective.basis: TCG release of the printing carrying the 'face-down Defense Position' text (SRL-EN040, Spell Ruler 25th Anniversary Edition)

event.historical_text: Discard 2 cards from your hand. Select 1 face-up monster and flip it face-down, but do not change its battle position.
event.modern_text: Discard 2 cards from your hand. Select 1 face-up monster and change it to face-down Defense Position.
event.summary: Functional erratum: the historical card flips the chosen monster face-down without changing its battle position - pre-errata/c511003028.lua calls Duel.ChangePosition(tc,POS_FACEDOWN_ATTACK,0,POS_FACEDOWN_DEFENSE,0), so a face-up Attack Position monster becomes face-down ATTACK Position - matching v1's 'flip it face-down, but do not change its battle position'. The modern script calls Duel.ChangePosition(tc,POS_FACEDOWN_DEFENSE) unconditionally, matching v2's 'change it to face-down Defense Position'. EdisonFormat.com records the same era behaviour and notes that such a monster cannot attack but can be Flip Summoned.

rulings_check.difference: The era card flips the chosen face-up monster face-down without changing its battle position (face-up Attack Position becomes face-down ATTACK Position); the modern card turns it into face-down Defense Position.
